body:
On a side note, I'm getting an error in my own project when running the project:
```
ERROR: Cannot instantiate C# script because the associated class could not be found. Script: 'csharp://Abstract/Data/WeightedList.cs:Abstract.Data.WeightedList`1[Turrets.TurretBlueprint].cs'. Make sure the script exists and contains a class definition with a name that matches the filename of the script exactly (it's case-sensitive).
```
And I'm not sure if it's related as I can't properly reproduce it in an MRP, but wanted to mention it (not sure what the error is so not sure how to report it)

Your MRP seems to be broken. The `Box.tres` file only contains embedded sub-resources, including a `CSharpScript`, but C# scripts aren't supported as embedded resources. For comparison, please refer to `ExampleItem.tres` to see how a resource with an attached C# script should be structured (it uses `ext_resource` instead of `sub_resource`).

It's possible that the resource broke after making changes to the MRP while testing different Godot versions.

Additionally, the `node.tscn` scene doesn't contain a value for the `Box` property. And reading your _Steps to reproduce_, it looks like it was supposed to.

I tried fixing the MRP by recreating the `Box.tres` resource and assigning it in the `node.tscn` scene. And when I rebuild the project, I get this error on Godot 4.4.0-stable:

```
ERROR: Script class can only be set together with base class name
```

This is a known issue (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/103343) that has already been fixed (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106243). The fix will be included in 4.5-beta2.

Since I had to make changes to the MRP, I'm not entirely sure that it's the same issue you encountered, so I won't be closing this issue as a duplicate. But I encourage you to test Godot 4.5-beta2 once it's released (or making a custom build from `master`) to see if this resolves your issue.

Still, if you could re-verify your MRP to ensure it accurately reflects the issue you're experiencing and can reproduce it consistently. That'd be very helpful.

> On a side note, I'm getting an error in my own project when running the project:
> ```
> ERROR: Cannot instantiate C# script because the associated class could not be found. Script: 'csharp://Abstract/Data/WeightedList.cs:Abstract.Data.WeightedList`1[Turrets.TurretBlueprint].cs'. Make sure the script exists and contains a class definition with a name that matches the filename of the script exactly (it's case-sensitive).
> ```

I assume you checked already, but make sure that:
- The file `res://Abstract/Data/WeightedList.cs` exists and contains a class named `WeightedList<T>` in the namespace `Abstract.Data`.
- A file named `TurretBlueprint.cs` exists that contains a class named `TurretBlueprint` in the namespace `Turrets`.
- You didn't move these files or renamed these classes or their namespaces recently.

If everything looks correct on your end, it sounds like it could be related to the issue I mentioned above (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/103343) so it's likely it's been fixed.
Just a quick update, haven't forgotten about this, I'll try to get around to testing it, but just haven't opened Godot in the past month.
